clue.text: Portents are confounded by prayer

indicators.note: to be confounded is to be thrown into confusion, so the letters of the two words before it are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone frets that ominous signs are baffling their prayers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are' looks like the verb of the sentence but is fodder: the eleven letters of PORTENTS and ARE are reshuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin opening words of the Lord's Prayer became the name for that prayer itself.

clue.text: Discussion between friend and a retired churchman

parts.note: a pal is a friend

indicators.note: something retired has gone back, so the word for the churchman is written backwards

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a clergyman's title

explanation.surface: A conversation takes place between a friend and a clergyman who has stepped down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' suggests a churchman who has stopped working; here it is the reversal signal on the clergyman's title. 'between' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A palaver is long-winded talk or fuss, a drawn-out conversation.

clue.text: The judge who always does his best

explanation.surface: A conscientious magistrate is praised for always giving his all.
explanation.definitionFit: One who tries a case in court, and also a person who keeps on trying hard.

clue.text: Incandescent rage about reciprocal help

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for rage is placed around the other piece

parts.note: to rant is to rage

indicators.note: reciprocal means turned the other way, so the word for help is read backwards

parts.note: aid means help

explanation.surface: Fury burns over the question of mutual assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reciprocal' sounds like a description of the help, as in mutual aid; it is really the signal to read that word backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something glowing brightly, as with heat or light.

clue.text: Work after a short month in the autumn getting seafood

indicators.note: after puts the word for work behind the month in the answer

parts.words: a short month in the autumn
parts.note: Oct is the abbreviation of October, an autumn month
an opus is a work, especially of music

explanation.surface: Someone finishes a job one October and treats themselves to fish.
explanation.definitionFit: This eight-armed sea creature is eaten as food in many cuisines.

clue.text: Can take in the annual return to Paul for cover

indicators.note: to take in is to contain, so the word for can goes around the other letters

parts.note: a tin is a can
AR is the abbreviation for an annual return, the yearly filing a company makes
the name is used as it is

explanation.surface: A tin must hold Paul's yearly tax form before it is protected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a verb but is the noun TIN, opened to hold AR and PAUL.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarpaulin is a heavy waterproof sheet spread over things to protect them.

clue.text: About to leave the recorder to get the goods supplied again

indicators.note: to leave means to go away, so the letter for about is removed from the instrument

parts.note: taken as written: the recorder is a woodwind instrument
c, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: Someone about to give up their recorder plans to buy fresh stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to leave' reads as 'on the point of leaving', but 'About' is C, which leaves RECORDER.
explanation.definitionFit: To place another order is to have the same supplies sent once more.

clue.text: Many teamed up, but took their time

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, which crosswords take for many
allied means joined together in alliance

explanation.surface: A large group joined forces but moved slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: To dally is to dawdle or linger instead of hurrying.

clue.text: Knock back beer when there's chill in the air

parts.note: to down a drink is to knock it back
draught is beer drawn from the barrel

explanation.surface: Drink up your ale when the weather turns cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock back' and 'beer' sit together as a drinker's phrase, but give separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A downward current of cold air, as from a chimney or high window, is felt as a chill.

clue.text: Go on strike for dress

explanation.surface: Workers walk out, and someone asks what to wear for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers who down tools are said to come out; and a person's outfit or turnout is their attire.

clue.text: Tiny eye movements detected during game

parts.note: tiddly is informal British for very small
winks are quick closings of one eye

explanation.surface: Small flickers of the eye give someone away during a match.
explanation.walkthrough: TIDDLY is British slang for tiny (it can also mean slightly drunk).
explanation.definitionFit: A table pastime in which small discs are flicked into a cup.

clue.text: Hesitate to give hand signals to Rex

parts.note: to wave is to signal with the hand
R stands for Rex, Latin for king, as in royal signatures

explanation.surface: A driver dithers about signalling to a dog called Rex.
explanation.definitionFit: To waver is to be unsure and hold back from deciding.

clue.text: Lead a pup round and get clapped

indicators.note: round means turned about, so the letters of the words before it are rearranged

parts.note: the printed words are the fodder, but the setter's version must have held one more D than they show

explanation.surface: Walk the puppy round the ring and the crowd will cheer.
explanation.walkthrough: As printed, LEAD A PUP has one D too few; the setter's fodder needs a second D to make the nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Being applauded means receiving a round of claps from an audience.

clue.text: Party worker joins marines, despite being inactive

indicators.note: joins means links up with, here coming between the two pieces as a bridge

parts.note: a do is a party
the ant is the crossword's usual worker
RM stands for Royal Marines

explanation.surface: A party activist signs up with the Marines even though they are idle.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Marines are Britain's naval infantry. 'joins' has the marines link the party and the worker, sitting between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dormant is asleep or not active for now.

clue.text: Everyone agreed to carry clubs simultaneously

indicators.note: to carry is to hold, so the phrase for everyone agreed holds the letter for clubs

parts.note: all at one means everyone in agreement
C is the abbreviation for clubs, the card suit

explanation.surface: The whole group consented to bring golf clubs along together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clubs' suggests golf, but it is C from the card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing things together in a single moment means they happen at the same time.

clue.text: Second clear out for student of part of the eyeball

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the word clear is rearranged

parts.note: L is for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A second student is told to clear out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' shuffles CLEAR to CLERA; L is from the learner plate on a British student driver's car.
explanation.definitionFit: The sclera is the white outer coat of the eye, and this adjective describes it.

clue.text: Was of use when a few were sick

annotationWithheld.why: Was of use when a few were sick (7): AVAILED needs A + V + AILED, and nothing in the clue as held gives V; 'few' is not V (perhaps 'five' was meant)
annotationWithheld.clue: Was of use when a few were sick

clue.text: The master, in our opinion, is sour

parts.note: an ace is an expert, a master of a skill
to us means as it seems to us

explanation.surface: We think the headmaster is a grumpy man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The master' suggests a schoolmaster; it is ACE, an expert, followed by TO US.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetous means like vinegar, so acidic in taste.

clue.text: Physician needs work in Germany

definitions.note: the definition stands for a place in Germany

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor

indicators.note: to work something is to knead or shape it, so the letters of needs are reworked

explanation.surface: A doctor must find a job in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs work' reads as a requirement, but 'work' is the anagram signal on NEEDS.
explanation.definitionFit: This city on the Elbe, capital of Saxony, is a place found in that country.

clue.text: Employee looked for a tool

parts.note: a hand is a worker, as in farmhand
saw means looked at or observed

explanation.surface: A worker goes in search of an implement.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw used with one hand, for cutting wood, is a workshop implement.

clue.text: Hitler's deputy harboured east German entertainer

indicators.note: to harbour is to shelter, so the deputy's name goes around the German word

parts.note: Rudolf Hess was deputy leader of the Nazi Party
Ost is the German word for east

explanation.surface: A Nazi leader hid an East German performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'east German' suggests the old GDR; it is OST, German for east.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostess receives and looks after guests, so she entertains them.

clue.text: Ploy she used as a security device

indicators.note: used means worked over, so the letters of the two words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman tried a trick to protect her home.
explanation.definitionFit: A small peephole in a door lets someone check a caller before opening it.

clue.text: The magnitude of the sergeants' mess

indicators.note: a mess is a muddle, so the letters of the soldiers' word are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone marvels at the size of the sergeants' dining hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' reads as the army dining room but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Greatness and magnitude both mean great size or importance.

clue.text: Artist wants that old material

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
yon is an old word for that

explanation.surface: A painter is looking for an old fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Rayon is a smooth artificial fibre woven into cloth.

clue.text: Mature Rhode island inscriber

parts.note: RI is the abbreviation for the US state of Rhode Island
a pen is used to write or inscribe

explanation.surface: An older engraver from Rhode Island is described.
explanation.definitionFit: To ripen is to grow fully developed, as fruit does.

clue.text: God! Ned is prickly

parts.note: Thor is the Norse god of thunder
the name is used as it is

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that Ned is touchy.
explanation.definitionFit: Having thorns makes a stem spiky to the touch.

clue.text: Uses tactics that upset me initially

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the overturned word goes first
upset means overturned, so the word me is reversed

parts.note: ploys are tactics or manoeuvres

explanation.surface: Someone complains about tricks that annoyed them at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like 'annoyed', but it is the reversal signal, and 'initially' says the turned word comes at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: To employ something is to make use of it.

clue.text: Recovering one's wits as result of vision

explanation.surface: Someone comes to their senses thanks to eyesight.
explanation.definitionFit: To start acting sensibly again, and the sense of sight, one of the five faculties.
